[Tutorial] Replace the whoaverse mascot with your own image and a link it wherever you like.

As always with CSS, you have to get creative!

Method 1

Replace the < img> tag with your own content

#header-img { content: url(< YOUR IMAGE LOCATION HERE >); }

So easy , but it only works with Chrome/Opera and other browsers that use Google's blink layout engine.

No effect on Firefox or IE.

Method 2

Has the same visual effect of replacing the image

Hide the img and add content before the pagename

#header-img {
 display: none; // remove the img from the page
}
span.pagename:before {
 background: url(< YOUR IMAGE LOCATION HERE >) no-repeat; // your image
 content: ""; // no text
 display: inline-block; // to allow correct page flow
 width: 113px; // the same size as the current
 height: 40px; // logo
 margin: 2px 5px 0px 0px; 
}

The problem is this removes the link so when you click the new image you don't go anywhere.

Method 3:

Place a link in your sidebar. [LINK TITLE](LINK URL)

Hide the img

Select ONLY the sidebar link and position it absolutely

Fix the positioning of the image

Fix the position of the tab menu 

#header-img {display:none}

 .side .md a[href="LINK URL"] { // target ONLY the single link - must match the URL of the link
 text-indent: -9999px; // hide the link text
 background: url(< YOUR IMAGE LOCATION HERE >) no-repeat; // this is your new image
 width: 113px; // image size
 height: 40px; // image size
 display: inline-block !important; // in order to push the tab menu over to the rigth
 position: absolute; // YUCK
 top: 109px; // image position on the page
 left: 20px; // image position on the page
 z-index: 9999; // make sure it's in front of everything else
}

#header-bottom-left {
 margin-left:142px; // need to give the tab menu some margins
 margin-top:110px; // to place it correctly 
}

About browsers

Method 2 and 3 work for Firefox and Chrome - so I guess it will work for Opera too.

Absolute positioning is a bad idea. I have an idea on how to fix this but I'm not at home yet.

Yes I agree, everything else floats behind things with absolute positioning. For example, the dropdown My Subverses list is behind the image :/

In fact I've thought of a simpler (probably better) way to achieve this:

First, make the the original image invisible;

#header-img { opacity:0 }

Then change the background of the bottom left header that contains the page name and tab menu to use your new image

#header-bottom-left {
 background-image:url(< YOUR IMAGE LOCATION HERE >);
 background-repeat: no-repeat;
 background-position: bottom left;
}

or use the compact form

#header-bottom-left {
 background:url(< YOUR IMAGE LOCATION HERE >) no-repeat bottom left;
}

Finally (Optional). If you added a sidebar link [LINK TITLE](LINK URL), position that link over the original image using absolute positioning - it's not visible and doesn't interfere with the other elements, it just provides the link over the top of the original image link.

.side .md a[href="LINK URL"] {
 text-indent: -9999px;
 width: 113px;
 height: 40px;
 display: inline-block !important;
 position: absolute;
 top: 109px;
 left: 20px;
 z-index: 9999;
}

I think this is better, although it still requires absolute positioning (to move the link from the sidebar), but it doesn't mess up the visible elements or page flow.

After some more experimenting it seems you can't move the link in the sidebar without ruining the drop down My Subverses menu.

And yes - it's the position: absolute that causes that to happen.

If you have any idea how to solve that problem I'd be very happy to know about it.
